articles.title: Charlie Tasker thriving during loan spell at Rochdale from Brighton
articles.excerpt: Charlie Tasker, on loan from Brighton, is making a strong impact at Rochdale, adapting well to a new position and earning the fans' support.
articles.content_html:
Charlie Tasker, a 20-year-old defender on loan from Brighton & Hove Albion, is quickly making his mark at Rochdale.

Since joining the League Two club, he has become a regular starter and has taken on a new role on the left side of defence, showcasing his adaptability and skill.

Tasker has expressed his excitement about his first loan experience, stating that he wanted to join a club where he would have a good chance of playing.

He noted that Rochdale's style of play is attractive and reminiscent of Brighton's, which has helped him settle in more easily.

The young defender has already garnered support from Rochdale fans, who appreciate his performances despite the team's recent 5-0 defeat at home.

Tasker has yet to return to his previous club in Mile Oak, indicating his commitment to making the most of his time in Rochdale.

As he continues to adapt to his new environment, Tasker is focused on contributing to Rochdale's success this season. His positive attitude and willingness to embrace the challenge of EFL football could prove beneficial for both him and the club moving forward.
articles.social_headline: Charlie Tasker is settling in well at Rochdale during his loan from Brighton.

articles.title: Road closures announced for Heywood Christmas Festival on 14 November 2026
articles.excerpt: Temporary road closures will affect several streets in Heywood during the Christmas Festival, as announced by Rochdale Borough Council.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced temporary road closures in Heywood for the Christmas Festival on 14 November 2026. The closures will impact several roads, ensuring a safe environment for festival attendees.

The specific roads affected include Bethel Street, where no waiting will be allowed at any time along its entire length. These measures are part of the council's efforts to facilitate the event and manage traffic effectively.

Residents and visitors should plan their journeys accordingly, as the closures may cause delays. The council encourages everyone to check for updates on roadworks and restrictions across Greater Manchester.

For more detailed information about the road closures and festival activities, residents can visit the Rochdale Borough Council's official website.

articles.title: Heywood’s Little Play Town put up for sale as owner reassures families it will stay open
articles.excerpt: Owner Jackie is seeking a buyer after four years, with Little Play Town remaining open and existing party bookings going ahead as planned.
articles.content_html:
Little Play Town in Heywood has been put up for sale, with owner Jackie reassuring families that the children’s role play business will remain open and existing party bookings will go ahead as planned.

Announcing the decision, Jackie said she was selling for personal reasons after four years of building the business alongside her team.

“This is something I never thought I’d be writing, and it’s been an incredibly difficult decision to make,” she said.

Jackie described Little Play Town as her “pride and joy” and thanked the staff, customers and families who have supported it.

She stressed that the sale announcement does not mean the venue is closing. Sessions will continue as normal, and families with parties booked do not need to change their plans.

The search is now on for a new owner to take over the established leasehold business. Jackie said a support package lasting up to three months would be available to help the buyer settle in.

The announcement highlights the existing staff team, supportive customer base and opportunities to introduce additional themed events, sessions and experiences. Jackie also described the landlord as proactive and supportive.

She hopes to find someone who will build on the business’s first four years and continue providing a place for children to play and make memories.

Anyone interested in buying Little Play Town can register their interest by emailing info@littleplaytownheywood.co.uk.

For local families, the immediate message is that the venue remains open and booked celebrations will continue as planned. What have your children enjoyed most about visiting Little Play Town? Share your memories in the comments.

articles.title: Steven's 15-stone weight loss transformation at Heywood Sports Village
articles.excerpt: Steven's remarkable journey to lose 15 stone has transformed his health and confidence, allowing him to enjoy life with his family.
articles.content_html:
Steven, a member of Heywood Sports Village, has achieved a remarkable transformation by losing 15 stone, significantly improving his health and quality of life. His journey began when he realised that everyday activities had become increasingly difficult, impacting his ability to enjoy family life.

At his heaviest, Steven struggled with simple tasks such as walking upstairs and playing with his children. The turning point came after witnessing his wife's successful health transformation, which inspired him to take control of his own wellbeing.

He sought guidance from Personal Trainer Alex at Heywood Sports Village, where he received structured training and nutritional support.

Throughout his journey, Steven faced challenges, including moments when motivation dipped. However, the support from his family and the gym community helped him stay focused on his long-term goals.

Today, he feels fitter, stronger, and more confident, enjoying activities that were once daunting. He can now buy clothes from regular high street shops and participate in family holidays without feeling self-conscious.

Steven advises others looking to start their fitness journey to make small changes and set clear personal goals. He emphasises the importance of seeking support and working with a coach to achieve lasting results.

His story serves as an inspiration for those in the community looking to improve their health.

articles.title: Middleton designated as mayoral development area to boost regeneration
articles.excerpt: Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig has designated Middleton as a mayoral development area, aiming to enhance economic development and housing in the town.
articles.content_html:
Middleton has been officially designated as a mayoral development area by Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig, marking a significant step forward in the town's regeneration efforts.

This decision follows a six-week public consultation and was approved by the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) last month, with Rochdale Council also endorsing the proposal.

The establishment of the Middleton Co-operative Mayoral Development Corporation is expected to accelerate economic development and regeneration in the area. The GMCA highlighted that this designation presents a substantial opportunity to improve Middleton town centre and its surrounding communities.

The new development corporation aims to attract both public and private investment, facilitating the construction of approximately 1,500 new homes, including affordable housing. This initiative is part of a broader strategy to enhance the living conditions and economic prospects for local residents.

The Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government has been notified of this designation, which will be formalised by an official order.

This development is crucial for Middleton, as it seeks to revitalise the town and provide much-needed housing and services for its community.

evidence_sources.captured_text: Town’s regeneration journey takes another step forward - Rochdale Times Skip to content LATEST NEWS Town’s regeneration journey takes another step forward Regeneration of Middleton has moved a step closer after the town was identified as a mayoral development area by Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig. Following a six-week public consultation, a report was submitted to a meeting of the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) last month when the proposed designation was approved and subsequently endorsed by Rochdale Council. The Mayor notified the Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government of the designation. The Secretary of State will, by Order, establish a Mayoral development corporation for the Area. The name to be given to the Mayoral development corporation is the Middleton Co-operative Mayoral Development Corporation. Designating the town as a mayoral development corporation is expected to help speed up furthering economic development and regeneration in Middleton. The GMCA said: “The area presents a significant opportunity to improve Middleton town centre and its surrounding communities. “Establishing the Middleton Co-operative Mayoral Development Corporation will help attract public and private investment, bring forward new development and support the delivery of around 1,500 new homes, including affordable homes. READ MORE: New trial gives children better mental health and social care support Middleton has been identified as a mayoral development area. Image: GMCA “It will also strengthen the town’s commercial and leisure offer, improve public spaces and infrastructure, create jobs and support better services for local people. “Without a dedicated delivery vehicle, Middleton would risk missing the opportunity to coordinate investment, accelerate regeneration and overcome barriers relating to land, infrastructure, viability, funding and delivery.” The corporation will be underpinned by co-operative principles, giving residents, businesses and community organisations a meaningful voice in shaping the regeneration programme. This approach will help ensure that investment delivers inclusive growth, social wellbeing, community pride and benefits that extend across Middleton and the wider borough. The corporation is expected to be established in early 2027. It will provide a single, focused body for local decision-making and engagement with residents, communities, government departments, public agencies, landowners, developers and investors. Working alongside Rochdale Council, Rochdale Development Agency and GMCA, it will coordinate delivery and help secure public and private investment to realise the shared vision for regeneration across the Area. articles.title: Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC partners with Gymbound for new gym and sponsorship
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC has unveiled a partnership with Gymbound, enhancing fitness for players and promoting community health initiatives.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC has announced a new partnership with Gymbound, which will see the launch of a new gym facility aimed at improving player fitness and conditioning.

This collaboration will also feature Gymbound's branding on the club's playing kits for the 2027 and 2028 seasons, marking a significant step in the club's development.

The partnership is designed to encourage greater participation in physical activity within the community, aligning with Rochdale Mayfield's goal to be the best amateur sports club in the borough.

The club, which boasts 17 teams including Women’s Masters and Disability Rugby League teams, aims to enhance its facilities and support for all players.

Carl Abraham, a representative from Rochdale Mayfield, highlighted the importance of this initiative, stating that it goes beyond mere branding and focuses on health and wellbeing.

The sponsorship will cover the playing kit programme for both upcoming seasons, ensuring that all teams from the youngest to the senior levels are equipped with the new kits.

As Rochdale Mayfield prepares to celebrate its 70th anniversary in 2028, this partnership with Gymbound represents a commitment to fostering a healthier community and improving the overall fitness of its players. Future health and community initiatives are also planned as part of this collaboration.

Gymbound will become the club’s official club-wide main shirt sponsor, with its branding set to feature on the front of playing shirts across every section of the club, from its youngest players through to its senior teams as Rochdale Mayfield prepares to celebrate its historic 70th anniversary in 2028. The agreement will also see Gymbound, in Eagle Technology Park, Queensway, support Rochdale Mayfield’s open-age pre-season training programme, providing players with access to a modern fitness environment to help improve strength, conditioning, fitness and overall preparation ahead of the new season. The partnership will introduce exclusive membership opportunities for Rochdale Mayfield players and club members, encouraging greater participation in physical activity and making fitness more accessible. Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC founder Carl Abraham said: “We are absolutely delighted to welcome Gymbound on board as our club-wide main shirt sponsor for the 2027 and 2028 seasons. “This is a significant partnership for Rochdale Mayfield and another major step forward in our ambition to become the best amateur sports club in the borough. “As a club, we are constantly looking to build relationships with local businesses that share our values, ambitions and commitment to the community. Gymbound is a fantastic example of that. “What makes this partnership particularly exciting is that it goes far beyond simply having a company’s name on our playing shirts. The support Gymbound will provide through our open-age pre-season programme, alongside exclusive membership opportunities for our players and members, demonstrates a genuine commitment to investing in the health, fitness and wellbeing of our club. “With hundreds of players representing Rochdale Mayfield, partnerships of this nature are vital in helping us continue to grow, improve our facilities and provide opportunities for people of all ages and abilities. “As we build towards our 70th anniversary in 2028, we want to ensure the club is in the strongest possible position, both on and off the field. “On behalf of everyone at Rochdale Mayfield, I would like to personally thank Chris and the team at Gymbound for their generosity, confidence in our vision and commitment to becoming part of the Mayfield family. “This is about two ambitious local organisations working together, supporting one another and making a positive difference in our community.” READ MORE: Town’s regeneration journey takes another step forward Gymbound will sponsor Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC shirts for two years. Image: Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC Chris Mason, owner of Gymbound, said: “As a new fitness facility in Rochdale, we wanted to establish ourselves as more than just another gym. Our ambition has always been to become part of the local community, helping people of all ages and abilities improve their health, fitness and overall wellbeing. “Rochdale Mayfield is a fantastic community club with a proud history, strong values and exciting ambitions for the future. “Having been good friends with Carl for many years, I’ve seen first-hand the incredible amount of hard work, dedication and commitment that goes on behind the scenes to make the club what it is today. “What really stands out is the opportunities Rochdale Mayfield provides for hundreds of people of all ages and abilities across the Borough. It’s much more than just a rugby league club; it’s a place that brings people together, creates opportunities and makes a genuine difference within the local community. “When we looked at what the club is achieving and, more importantly, its ambitions for the future, we knew Gymbound wanted to be part of that journey. “For us, this partnership is about much more than having the Gymbound name on the front of a rugby shirt. “We are particularly excited to support the club’s open-age pre-season training programme and introduce exclusive membership opportunities that will benefit Mayfield players and members. “We see this as the beginning of a long-term relationship where both organisations can grow together, support one another and make a genuine difference within the Rochdale community. “We are looking forward to welcoming Rochdale Mayfield into Gymbound and playing our part in what promises to be an exciting period for the club as it approaches its 70th anniversary. “Two organisations with shared values, a passion for fitness and a commitment to our local community.” Established in 1958, Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC now has 17 teams and opportunities for participants aged from just three years old through to those in their 70s. Alongside its traditional rugby league teams, Rochdale Mayfield continues to develop its Women’s Masters, Disability Rugby League and community wellbeing programmes. The incident occurred while Whelan was working at the site, although specific details regarding the circumstances of the incident have not been disclosed. Emergency services were not mentioned in the reports, and it remains unclear what immediate actions were taken following the incident.

Whelan's family has shared their grief publicly, highlighting the impact of his loss on their lives. They remember him fondly, reflecting on his character and contributions as a family member and worker.

This incident highlights the critical importance of safety measures in roadside work environments. Ensuring proper safety protocols is essential to prevent such tragedies in the future.

articles.title: Eight winners honoured at Rochdale Diversity Awards 2026
articles.excerpt: The Rochdale Diversity Awards celebrated eight winners for their contributions to equality and community cohesion at a ceremony attended by over 350 guests.
articles.content_html:
More than 350 guests gathered at Rochdale Town Hall on October 30, 2026, for the Rochdale Diversity Awards, which recognised eight winners for their outstanding contributions to equality, diversity, and community cohesion across the borough.

Organised by the Kashmir Youth Project (KYP), the awards celebrated the achievements of individuals and organisations that have made significant impacts in promoting inclusivity. This year, the event received over 130 nominations, showcasing the breadth of community engagement in Rochdale.

Among the winners, Rochdale Science Initiative C.I.C. received the Breaking Barriers Award, while its founder, Mohammed Attaur Rahman, was honoured with the Outstanding Achievement in Diversity Award.

Other notable recognitions included the Diversity in Public Sector Partnership Working Award, awarded to Petrus and the Rochdale Community Safety Team for their Town Centre Outreach Initiative.

The awards, which KYP has delivered since 2012, highlight the importance of fostering a diverse and inclusive community. The recognition of these efforts not only celebrates individual achievements but also encourages ongoing commitment to equality and cohesion in Rochdale.

articles.title: Sir Ian McKellen to headline event at Factory International in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Sir Ian McKellen is set to headline an event at Factory International in Rochdale, as part of a broader initiative to reshape local public spaces into cultural hubs. This event, scheduled for October 31, aims to engage the community in discussions about transforming parks, libraries, and other public areas.
articles.content_html:
Sir Ian McKellen is set to headline an event at Factory International in Rochdale on October 31, as part of a broader initiative to reshape local public spaces into cultural hubs.

This event aims to engage the community in discussions about transforming parks, libraries, and other public areas into accessible venues for cultural and creative activities.

The initiative invites local residents and partners to share their ideas on enhancing these spaces, which are envisioned as vibrant community assets. This effort builds on previous discussions about 'Third Spaces' and 'Everyday Utopias', concepts that encourage community gathering and creative expression.

The Rochdale Development Agency, in collaboration with Rochdale Borough Council and the cultural compact Rochdale Creates, is developing a new 'Cultural, Creative and Heritage Asset Strategy'.

This strategy will guide the transformation of local spaces based on community input gathered during the event, ensuring that the voices of residents are heard in shaping their environment.

This initiative is significant for residents as it aims to foster a sense of belonging and community engagement through cultural activities. The discussions will contribute to long-term strategies for the borough's libraries and green spaces, ensuring they serve as vibrant community assets.
articles.social_headline: Sir Ian McKellen to lead community discussions on reshaping Rochdale's public spaces.

articles.title: Former police officer sacked for sharing confidential information with Rochdale drug dealer
articles.excerpt: Tubah Hamid, a former Tameside police officer, was dismissed after breaching confidentiality by sharing police information with her Rochdale drug dealer partner.
articles.content_html:
Tubah Hamid, a former police officer with Greater Manchester Police, was dismissed after an accelerated misconduct hearing found she had shared confidential police information with her partner, who is linked to an organised crime group in Rochdale.

The hearing, presided over by Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson, concluded that Hamid's actions constituted gross misconduct due to multiple breaches of professional standards.

The misconduct hearing revealed that Hamid's behaviour included unlawful access to police data over an extended period, which was described as 'deliberate and persistent'. Sir Stephen stated that her culpability was 'very high', highlighting a significant abuse of her position and a lack of integrity.

As a result of her actions, Hamid was dismissed with immediate effect and her name has been added to the College of Policing's Barred List, preventing her from serving in any police role in the future.

The disciplinary proceedings followed a criminal investigation into her conduct, which raised serious concerns about her suitability for the role of constable.

This case highlights the critical importance of integrity and accountability within the police force, particularly in maintaining public trust. The dismissal of Tubah Hamid serves as a significant reminder of the consequences of misconduct within law enforcement.
articles.social_headline: Tubah Hamid dismissed for sharing police secrets with Rochdale drug dealer.
